correctness.rationale: The forward-time theorem is correct but the frozen Finding and Assumptions do not constrain t to be nonnegative. In the proof the claim that the slope is negative silently uses t>0. Reflecting the spectrum via A*= (L+μ)I−A preserves the Krylov space, and in a common orthonormal basis reflects the compression by the same affine formula. Thus y₂(−s;A*,b)=exp(s(L+μ))y₂(s;A,b). Reflect the frozen positive-time witness to A*=diag(3,14/5,1), b=(1,1,1/100), t=−1. With μ=1 and L=3 the written bound t(L−μ)≤1 holds, but the third component is approximately −0.15749287. Independent evaluation used the roots of the degree-two orthogonal polynomial for the spectral measure with weights bᵢ² as Ritz values and evaluated the interpolation line directly. For t≥0, the MVT controls right extrapolation by the derivative at the lower Ritz value and proves sufficiency including equality. Two distinct active eigenvalues just above the lower endpoint, then a small positive weight at the upper endpoint, give the stated negative example for every t(L−μ)>1. With at most two active eigenvalues, including early breakdown, the space is invariant and the action is exact; t=0 and L=μ are also exact. In an unrestricted real-time statement the correct bound is |t|(L−μ)≤1. Even with an implicit forward-time convention, the originality disposition is unchanged.
residual_risks: The numerical evaluation is illustrative; the counterexample for unrestricted t also follows exactly by reflection from forward sharpness. Exact arithmetic and diagonal matrices only.
